id_and_class.theory_title: Whitehead's Experience is Fundamental, Consciousness is Not
id_and_class.summary: Alfred North Whitehead held that reality is made of momentary ‘actual occasions’ of experience, each formed by feeling (prehending) the occasions before it, so experience is everywhere actuality is. Consciousness is rare, late and derivative: it is the way a high-grade occasion feels the contrast between what is the case and what might have been. The hard problem changes shape, since nothing has to produce experience from wholly non-experiential matter; the question becomes why awareness is so rare.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as the Rare Crown of Universal Experience

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is the subjective form of an intellectual feeling, the way an occasion feels the ‘affirmation-negation contrast’ between a given fact and an alternative possibility. Experience in general is prehension, the taking account of data, and most of it is nonconscious.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Mental and physical are two poles of every occasion within one process, not two substances. A human mind is a stream of high-grade occasions closely integrated with the living body, so mind-body interaction needs no special bridge, prehension being the one relation throughout nature.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Consciousness emerges from experience, never experience from the non-experiential; experience itself is fundamental
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Every occasion is a subject while it becomes and then perishes into an object for its successors. Whitehead calls this ‘subjective form,’ the how of a feeling rather than its what, and it is present throughout nature; reflective awareness is not.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Qualities such as greenness and warmth belong to nature itself rather than being added by an observer; Whitehead rejects the ‘bifurcation of nature’ that makes them inexplicable residue. He does not explain why high-grade experience has the specific qualities humans report.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Actual occasions, prehensions, eternal objects (pure possibilities), creativity as the ultimate principle, and God as an actual entity whose primordial nature holds eternal objects and supplies each occasion's initial aim.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Metaphysical construction answerable to experience; Whitehead warns that introspection favors the clear, recent and articulable and misses the mass of inherited feeling behind it.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Occasions grow together (‘concrescence’) in phases: physical feelings take in past actualities, conceptual feelings add possibilities, and later phases integrate them until the occasion reaches ‘satisfaction.’ Occasions form societies, some of them compound individuals with a presiding occasion.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Experience in general, phenomenal awareness, novelty, judgment, imagination, decision, unity of mind and the combination problem.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Intellectual feeling integrates a physical feeling of an actual state of affairs with a propositional feeling of how it might be otherwise; consciousness is how that contrast is felt.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Consciousness arises only in late phases of some occasions' becoming and is episodic; the earlier phases that produce it never enter it.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Experience is present in every actual occasion; consciousness only in high-grade occasions such as those presiding over animal bodies. Aggregates like rocks have experiencing parts but no experience of the whole.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Consciousness is a specialized instrument for novel situations that demand conceptual contrast and decision; routine functioning, including most of our own, goes on without it.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: A dominant occasion prehends and integrates contributions from brain and body. The unified conscious occasion is numerically distinct from the bodily occasions it draws on, so many subjects need not sum into one.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Each occasion inherits its causal past through prehensions, selectively including data (positive prehensions) or excluding them (negative prehensions), and on completion becomes a datum for successors.
core_claims_and_evidence: ‘Consciousness presupposes experience, and not experience consciousness’: most experience is nonconscious.
Nothing actual is wholly devoid of experience; Whitehead rejects ‘vacuous actuality’ and the fallacy of misplaced concreteness.
Consciousness occupies only a narrow focal region of a much larger experience, so the simplicity of what we notice is no measure of the whole.
God supplies each occasion's initial aim, the relevant possibility that gives its becoming direction, and later retains completed occasions as data.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Basile argues that integration by a dominant occasion restates the combination problem rather than solving it. Critics also say that attributing experience to an electron names the problem without solving it, and that Whitehead's technical use of ‘feeling’ lets metaphor carry the explanation.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: The theory has no quantitative laws, no criteria for finding presiding occasions in brains, and no distinctive predictions. It assumes rather than shows that elementary processes experience, and its eternal objects and God cannot simply be dropped.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: The system is internally integrated and rejects both substance dualism and reductive materialism. Whether it is a panpsychism is disputed: Whitehead was evasive when asked, Griffin prefers ‘panexperientialism,’ and Basile reads him as a panpsychist. God's primordial consciousness is a further disputed case.

AI_consciousness.rationale: On this view a whole is conscious only if it has a presiding occasion; a machine that is a mere aggregate would have experiencing parts but no consciousness of its own.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since the mind is a stream of occasions bound to the living body and each perishes as a subject, personal survival does not follow; Whitehead offers instead ‘objective immortality,’ in which God retains completed occasions as data.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: God gives every occasion its initial aim toward novelty and preserves achieved value, and Whitehead calls God the great companion, the fellow-sufferer who understands.
